references.text: The same chapter uses the expression 'reject my statutes' (מָאֲסוּ בְּחֻקֹּתַי) and describes Israel's breach of the covenant.
Israel rejected (וַיִּמְאֲסוּ) the Lord's statutes and his covenant, using the same terminology as in Leviticus 26:15.
Isaiah uses the same expression regarding rejecting (מָאֲסוּ) the Lord's law and despising the words of the Holy One.
Jeremiah speaks of how the fathers broke the covenant (הֵפֵרוּ אֶת־בְּרִיתִי), using the same expression as 'break my covenant' in Leviticus.
The Lord speaks of the covenant that Israel broke (הֵפֵרוּ אֶת־בְּרִיתִי), a direct parallel to the breach of covenant in Leviticus 26:15.
Ezekiel describes Israel as having rejected the Lord's judgments (בְּמִשְׁפָּטַי מָאָסוּ), using the same terms as in Leviticus 26:15.
Moses predicts that Israel will reject the Lord and break the covenant, addressing the same theme of covenant breach.
The psalmist speaks of rejecting the Lord's statutes and breaking his commands, yet the Lord will not break his covenant.
Hebrews refers to the consequences of rejecting the Mosaic law and trampling underfoot the blood of God's Son.
